source_text: ίεμεν γὰρ τοῖς ἁγίοις, οὐχ ἑτέρου του χάριν, ἢ ὥστε μεταλαχεῖν τοῦ ἁγίου Χριστοῦ διά τε τῆς ἀποῤῥήτου καὶ πνευματικῆς θυσίας. Διαγνίζεται δὲ καὶ τὰ ταῖς θυσίαις ὑπηρετοῦντα σκεύη, ὡς ἂν μὴ ἑτέρῳ γένοιτό τινι, μηδὲ ταῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὑποφέροιτο χρείαις τὰ τοῖς ἱεροῖς λελειτουργηκότα. Τετήρηται δὲ ὁ νόμος, καὶ ἐν ἐκκλησίαις σώζεται. Ἀνδριζομένοις δὲ ὅτι τὸ εὐλογεῖσθαι πρέπει, σαφηνιεῖ πάλιν ὁ νόμος εἰπών· «Πᾶν ἄρσεν ἐν τοῖς ἱερεῦσι φάγεται αὐτά.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Σαφὴς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Θεσμοθετεῖ δὲ πρὸς τούτοις, καὶ ὅπως ἂν γένοιτο καλῶς τῆς θυσίας ὁ τρόπος, τῆς ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας, φημί· καὶ τίνα μὲν ἐξ αὐτῆς, τὰ τοῖς λειτουργοῦσιν ἐδώδιμα, τίνα δὲ αὖ, τὰ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἐξῃρημένα. Γέγραπται γὰρ οὕτω· «Καὶ πάντα, φησὶ, τὰ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὧν ἂν εἰσενεχθῇ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῶν εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐξιλάσασθαι ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ, οὐ βρωθήσεται, ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται. Καὶ οὗτος ὁ νόμος τοῦ κριοῦ τοῦ περὶ τῆς πλημμελείας, Ἅγια ἁγίων ἐστίν· ἐν τόπῳ οὗ σφάξουσι τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα, σφάξουσι τὸν κριὸν περὶ τῆς πλημμελείας ἔναντι Κυρίου. Καὶ τὸ αἷμα προσχεεῖ ἐπὶ τὴν βάσιν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου κύκλῳ· καὶ πᾶν τὸ στέαρ αὐτοῦ προσοίσει ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν, καὶ πᾶν τὸ στέαρ τὸ κατακαλύπτον τὰ ἐνδόσθια, καὶ πᾶν τὸ στέαρ τὸ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐνδοσθίων· καὶ τοὺς δύο νεφροὺς, καὶ τὸ στέαρ τὸ ἐπ' αὐτῶν τὸ ἐπὶ τῶν μηρίων, καὶ τὸν λοβὸν τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ ἥπατος σὺν τοῖς νεφροῖς, περιελεῖ αὐτὰ, καὶ ἀνοίσει αὐτὰ ὁ ἱερεὺς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κάρπωμα τῷ Κυρίῳ· περὶ πλημμελείας ἐστί. Πᾶς ἄρσην ἐκ τῶν ἱερέων ἔδεται αὐτὰ, ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ ἔδονται αὐτά. Ἅγια ἁγίων ἐστίν. Ὥσπερ τὸ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, οὕτω καὶ τὸ περὶ τῆς πλημμελείας· νόμος εἷς αὐτῶν ὁ ἱερεὺς ὅστις ἐξιλάσεται ἐν αὐτῷ, αὐτῷ ἔσται.» Ἀποφάσκει μὲν γὰρ δεῖν ποιεῖσθαι τροφὰς τὰ τῶν ἱερείων ἐνδόσθια. Χρὴ γὰρ μόνῳ, φησὶν, ἀνακεῖσθαι Θεῷ, καὶ αὐτῷ προσάγεσθαι· τουτὶ γὰρ οἶμαι καταδηλοῦν τὸ, «ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται,» τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἀνακεῖσθαι τὸ ἐν μόνῃ ἐκνενεμήσθω σαφῶς τῇ θείᾳ τε καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντα φύσει, ἧς εἰς τύπον τὸ πῦρ. Καταθυομένου δὲ τοῦ κριοῦ τῆς πλημμελείας, προσχεῖται τὸ αἷμα τῇ βάσει τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου· ἅγιος γὰρ καὶ ἱερὸς ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, καὶ μὴν καὶ εὐώδης. Ἀναφέρεται γὰρ τὰ ἐνδόσθια, πιμελὴ, καὶ νεφροὶ, καὶ λοβὸς τοῦ ἥπατος. Εἶεν δ' ἂν, οἶμαι, ταυτὶ, καθὰ καὶ ἐν ἑτέροις ἔφην, εἰς ἀρετῆς τύπον τῆς οὐ μιᾶς, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν εἴδει πολλῶν. Πλεῖστοι γὰρ ὅσοι τῆς ἀρετῆς οἱ τρόποι· δεδικαιώμεθα δὴ οὖν ἐν Χριστῷ, τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀνατλάντι θάνατον, καὶ ἀναθέντι ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί· ὅτι δὲ οὐκ ἀμισθὶ λειτουργήσομεν τῷ Θεῷ, σαφηνίζει, λέγων εὐθύς τε καὶ ἐφεξῆς· «Καὶ ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ προσάγων ὁλοκαυτώματα ἀνθρώπου, τὸ δέρμα τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως ἧς αὐτὸς προσφέρει, αὐτῷ ἔσται, καὶ πᾶσα θυσία ἥτις ποιηθήσεται ἐν τῷ κλιβάνῳ. Καὶ πᾶσα ἥτις ποιηθήσεται
pass_a_gloss: [we draw] near to the holy things for no other reason than to share in the holy Christ through the ineffable and spiritual sacrifice. And the vessels serving the sacrifices are also thoroughly purified, so that the things that have ministered to the sacred things might not come to anyone else, nor be brought under the uses of men. And the law has been kept, and is preserved in churches. And that being blessed befits those who play the man, the law will make clear again, saying: 'Every male among the priests shall eat them.' PALL.: The account is clear. CYR.: And he lays down besides these also how the manner of the sacrifice might well come about, of the one for sin, I mean; and which things from it are eatable for the ministers, and which again are set apart for an odour of fragrance. For it is written thus: 'And all the sin offerings, he says, of which some of their blood is brought into the tent of witness to make atonement in a holy place, shall not be eaten; it shall be burned up in fire. And this is the law of the ram for the trespass; it is holy of holies; in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering they shall slaughter the ram for the trespass before the Lord. And he shall pour the blood at the base of the altar round about; and he shall offer all its fat from it, and the loin, and all the fat covering the inward parts, and all the fat on the inward parts; and the two kidneys, and the fat on them, the one on the thighs, and the lobe on the liver with the kidneys, he shall take them away, and the priest shall bring them up upon the altar as an offering to the Lord; it is for trespass. Every male of the priests shall eat them, in a holy place they shall eat them; it is holy of holies. As the sin offering, so also the trespass offering; one law of them: the priest who shall make atonement with it, it shall be his.' For he denies that the inward parts of the victims must be made food. For they must, he says, be dedicated to God alone and brought to him; for this, I think, is what is shown by 'it shall be burned up in fire,' that is, let the being dedicated be clearly allotted to the divine nature alone that is above all, of which fire is a type. And when the ram of the trespass is sacrificed, the blood is poured at the base of the altar; for the death of Christ is holy and sacred, and indeed also fragrant. For the inward parts are brought up, fat, and kidneys, and lobe of the liver. And these would be, I think, as I said in other places too, for a type of virtue not single, but as in the form of many. For very many are the ways of virtue; so then we have been justified in Christ, who endured death for us and dedicated himself for an odour of fragrance to God and the Father; and that we shall not minister to God without wage, he makes clear, saying straightway and next: 'And the priest who offers a man's whole burnt offerings, the skin of the whole burnt offering which he himself offers shall be his, and every sacrifice which shall be made in the oven. And every one which shall be made
pass_b_english: Cyril: …to the holy things for no other reason than to share in the holy Christ through the ineffable and spiritual sacrifice. And the vessels that serve the sacrifices are also purified (Leviticus 6:28), so that what has served sacred things may belong to nothing else and not be put to human uses. This law has been kept, and it is preserved in the churches. And the law will again make clear that being blessed befits those who act with manly courage, when it says: ‘Every male among the priests shall eat them’ (Leviticus 6:29).

Cyril: Besides this, he also lays down how the sacrifice should be properly carried out (the sacrifice for sin, I mean): which parts of it the ministers may eat, and which are set apart for a fragrant aroma. For it is written thus: ‘And all the sin offerings, any of whose blood is brought into the tent of witness to make atonement in the holy place, shall not be eaten; it shall be burned up in fire (Leviticus 6:30). And this is the law of the ram of the guilt offering; it is most holy. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord. And he shall pour its blood at the base of the altar all around. And he shall offer from it all its fat: the loin, and all the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat on the entrails, and the two kidneys and the fat on them that is on the thighs, and the lobe on the liver with the kidneys; he shall remove them, and the priest shall offer them on the altar as an offering to the Lord; it is a guilt offering. Every male of the priests shall eat them; they shall eat them in a holy place; they are most holy. As the sin offering is, so is the guilt offering; there is one law for them. The priest who makes atonement with it shall have it’ (Leviticus 7:1–7).

For he declares that the inward parts of the victims must not be made into food. They must, he says, be dedicated to God alone and offered to him. This, I think, is what ‘it shall be burned up in fire’ points to; that is, what is dedicated is to be plainly assigned to the divine nature alone, which is above all things, and of which fire is a type. And when the ram of the guilt offering is sacrificed, its blood is poured out at the base of the altar; for the death of Christ is holy and sacred, and fragrant as well. For the inward parts are offered up: the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver. These, I think, as I have said elsewhere too, would be a type of virtue, not of one virtue only but of many kinds. For the ways of virtue are very many. And so we have been justified in Christ, who endured death for us and dedicated himself to God the Father as a fragrant aroma (Ephesians 5:2).

He makes clear that we shall not serve God without reward, for he says straight after this: ‘And the priest who offers someone’s whole burnt offering, the skin of the whole burnt offering that he offers shall be his; and every sacrifice that is prepared in the oven, and every one that is prepared…’ (Leviticus 7:8–9)

choices.why: 'ὀσφύς' rendered 'loin' following the LXX (Hebrew: the fat tail).
'ἐνδόσθια' in Cyril's comment: he seems to extend the burned sin offering (6:30) to the inward parts set apart for God in 7:3-5; translated literally as 'inward parts'.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-word: 'Προσ' at the end of §25 + 'ίεμεν' here = 'we draw near'. Ends mid-quotation; Leviticus 7:9 continues in §27 ('…on a grill or in a pan'). Leviticus 6:30 in English numbering is LXX 6:23 (Rahlfs). 'κριὸς τῆς πλημμελείας' follows the LXX, which supplies 'ram' at Leviticus 7:1 where the Hebrew has only 'guilt offering'. 'ὀσφύς' rendered 'loin' following the LXX (Hebrew: the fat tail). 'κάρπωμα' rendered 'an offering'. The clause 'τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἀνακεῖσθαι τὸ ἐν μόνῃ ἐκνενεμήσθω σαφῶς τῇ θείᾳ… φύσει' is grammatically rough in the Migne text (likely corrupt); rendered by its evident sense: what is dedicated is assigned to the divine nature alone, of which fire is a type. 'ἐνδόσθια' in Cyril's comment: he seems to extend the burned sin offering (6:30) to the inward parts set apart for God in 7:3-5; translated literally as 'inward parts'. 'Ἀνδριζομένοις' (acting manfully) may echo 1 Corinthians 16:13 (ἀνδρίζεσθε) but this is doubtful; uncited. 'δεδικαιώμεθα ἐν Χριστῷ' is Pauline language (cf. Galatians 2:17; Romans 5:9) without a single clear source; uncited. The fragrant self-offering to God the Father matches Ephesians 5:2 (προσφορὰν καὶ θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας), cited.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [Προσ]ίεμεν (we approach) τοῖς ἁγίοις for no other reason than μεταλαχεῖν (to partake) of the ἅγιος Χριστός through the ἀπόρρητος (ineffable) and πνευματική θυσία. The σκεύη serving the sacrifices διαγνίζεται (are thoroughly purified), so that what λελειτουργηκότα (has served) the sacred things should not belong to anything else nor be put under human χρεῖαι (uses). The νόμος τετήρηται (has been kept) and σώζεται ἐν ἐκκλησίαις. That τὸ εὐλογεῖσθαι (being blessed) πρέπει (befits) ἀνδριζομένοις (those who act manfully), the law σαφηνιεῖ (will make clear) again: 'Πᾶν ἄρσεν among the priests shall eat them.' PALL.: Σαφὴς ὁ λόγος. CYR.: He θεσμοθετεῖ (lays down) also how ὁ τρόπος (the manner) of the θυσία ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας should be done καλῶς, which parts ἐδώδιμα (edible) for τοῖς λειτουργοῦσιν, which ἐξῃρημένα (set apart) εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας. Quote Lev 6:30 (LXX 6:23) + 7:1-7: sin offerings whose blood is εἰσενεχθῇ into the σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐξιλάσασθαι (to make atonement) in the holy place οὐ βρωθήσεται, ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται. Law of the κριός (ram) περὶ τῆς πλημμελείας (guilt/trespass); ἅγια ἁγίων; slaughtered where the ὁλοκαύτωμα is; blood προσχεεῖ (poured) at the βάσις of the θυσιαστήριον κύκλῳ; all the στέαρ (fat), the ὀσφύς (loin), fat covering the ἐνδόσθια (entrails), fat on the entrails, two νεφροί (kidneys) with fat on the μηρία (thighs), λοβὸς ἐπὶ τοῦ ἥπατος (lobe of the liver) with the kidneys, περιελεῖ (remove), the priest ἀνοίσει on the altar as κάρπωμα τῷ Κυρίῳ; every ἄρσην of the priests eats in a holy place; ἅγια ἁγίων; as the sin offering so the guilt offering, νόμος εἷς; the priest ὅστις ἐξιλάσεται with it, his it shall be. He ἀποφάσκει (denies) that the ἐνδόσθια of the ἱερεῖα may be made τροφαί (food): they must ἀνακεῖσθαι (be dedicated) to God alone and προσάγεσθαι to him; this, I think, καταδηλοῦν (shows) 'ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται', that is, [what is dedicated] ἐκνενεμήσθω (let it be assigned) clearly to the θεία καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντα φύσις alone, of which τὸ πῦρ is εἰς τύπον. When the κριὸς τῆς πλημμελείας is καταθυόμενος, the blood is poured at the base of the altar: for Christ's θάνατος is ἅγιος, ἱερός, εὐώδης. The ἐνδόσθια, πιμελή (fat), νεφροί, λοβός are ἀναφέρεται (offered up); these, I think, as I said ἐν ἑτέροις, are εἰς ἀρετῆς τύπον, not of one but ὡς ἐν εἴδει πολλῶν (as in the form of many). Πλεῖστοι οἱ τρόποι of ἀρετή; δεδικαιώμεθα (we have been justified) ἐν Χριστῷ, who ἀνατλάντι (endured) θάνατος for us and ἀναθέντι ἑαυτόν (dedicated himself) εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας to God and Father. That we shall not λειτουργήσομεν to God ἀμισθί (without wages), he σαφηνίζει, saying εὐθύς τε καὶ ἐφεξῆς: Lev 7:8-9, the priest offering ὁλοκαυτώματα ἀνθρώπου (anyone's whole burnt offerings): the δέρμα (skin) of the ὁλοκαύτωσις shall be his, and every θυσία made ἐν τῷ κλιβάνῳ (in the oven), and every one made [continued §27]…
